title: Answer: free will needs a non-computable factor, which orchestrated reduction may supply

statements.text: Orch OR holds that if algorithmic computation fully determined thought there would be no room for independent causal agency or free will, so something non-computable is needed, and it places that factor in orchestrated objective reduction. Each reduction is a choice between alternatives, and the temporal non-locality of entanglement within it may let conscious experience act on behavior despite its timing, giving consciousness causal efficacy and a semblance of free will rather than the role of an epiphenomenal illusion.
statements.scope: the 2014 review Consciousness in the universe

sources.quote: appears to preclude any possibility for independent causal agency, or free will. Something else is needed.

Accordingly, Orch OR could well enable consciousness to have a causal efficacy, despite its apparently anomalous relation to a timing assigned to it in relation to an external clock, thereby allowing conscious action to provide a semblance of free will
